panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Initial axial CT showing ground-glass opacities and reticulation, consistent with the onset of dendriform pulmonary ossification presentation. B: Follow-up axial CT showing progression of reticular opacities and traction bronchiectasis. C: Axial reconstruction explicitly showing interstitial calcifications compatible with dendriform pulmonary ossification (arrows). This is the characteristic finding. D: Coronal reconstruction explicitly showing interstitial calcifications compatible with dendriform pulmonary ossification (arrows). This is the characteristic finding.

panels.figure_caption: Axial computed tomography (CT) performed with lung window settings showed bilateral ground-glass opacities with mild reticulation (A). CT performed two months later demonstrated improvement of the ground-glass opacities but progression of the reticular opacities, with traction bronchiectasis on the anterior aspect of the superior lobes (B). Axial and coronal reconstructions acquired with mediastinal window settings showed interstitial calcifications compatible with dendriform pulmonary ossification over the reticular pattern (C and D,arrows).
in_text_mentions: oms. His condition progressed to acute respiratory failure, and he was placed on mechanical ventilation. Chest computed tomography (CT) showed bilateral ground-glass opacities with mild reticulation (Figure 1A). The patient was treated with supportive measures, including antibiotic therapy and corticosteroid therapy. He recovered well and was discharged. Two months later, he presented with worsening dyspnea and cough. A new CT showed improvement in the ground-glass opacities but a progression of the reticular opacities, with traction bronchiectasis on the anterior aspect of the superior lobes.

in_text_mentions: owed a value within normal range. Subsequently, the patient was subjected to bronchoscopy procedure with transbronchial biopsy, but it proved to be inconclusive to help forming a final diagnosis, as it was showing lymphoplasmacytic cell infiltration with dystrophic calcification. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Chest radiograph showing baseline findings of bilateral reticulonodular shadows in the lower lung zone, consistent with the documented case of dendriform pulmonary ossification. B: Chest radiograph showing evolution of findings, specifically the bilateral reticulonodular shadows in the lower lung zone, compared to panel A.
panels.attribution_text: Komatsu et al. Idiopathic Dendriform Pulmonary Ossification Diagnosed by Transbronchial Lung Cryobiopsy: A Case Report.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.77955. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Chest radiography findings over time (A) Chest radiograph at medical check-up. (B) The bilateral reticulonodular shadows in the lower lung zone (circle) became clearer after five years.
in_text_mentions: serum chemistry test results were within normal limits. Pulmonary function test results were normal: vital capacity of 4.85 L (105.4%), forced vital capacity of 4.86 L (109%), forced expiratory volume in 1 s of 3.52 L (94.4%), and diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide of 23.41 mL/min/mmHg (104%). Chest radiography showed deterioration over the five-year period, with bilateral reticulonodular shadows evident in the lower lung zone (Figure 1). Chest CT revealed bilateral, diffuse, linear, and branching structures with calcification, predominantly in the lower lung lobes (Figure 2).
